I'm trying to buy a nice pair of binoculars, what to look for?
Literally have no idea about binoculars. Just recently was told they can be used to look at stars.

you want full coated lens. this means that every viewing surface is coated with some different chemicals and treatments. next look at fully sealed with argon gas or nitrogen gas inside. this aides in clearity as well as keeping fog and condensation from forming inside the tubes.

next you have two types, porro prisms and roof prisms. porros are generally cheaper and the quality depends on the glass used. roof prisms are more expensive and are usually offered as premium. porro prisms binos are the ones with the wide set objective lenses. roof prism binos are two straight tubes.

next, magnification and obejective lenses. in general to get best exit pupil size and good low light visibilty you want the objective lenses to be no than 4 times the magnification power.(i say avoid any thing less than 3 times the magnification) so a 4 power (zoom) would great with objective lense of 24mm or greater. 12 power (zoom) is great with a 48mm or greater objective lense. the trade off is larger objective lenses weight more and and greater magnication with small objective lense gives a dark image with a very small exit pupil diameter. also take into consideration if you are going to keep them in your truck or at home for stantionary use or are you gonna be hiking all hunting game or serious bird watching.

the biggest percentage of your cost is paying for the glass in the tubes. an yes, there is a difference between $20, $100, $300 and $1,000 optics. go to the store and try out an 12x40 $50 pair of binos and then the 12x40 $300 pair of binos. take note of the brightness, the clarity the detail of objects and the edges of the field of view will have blurry edges or not have blurry edges.

oh. and the 12x40 means 12 times magnification (power) and the 40 is 40milimeter objective lenses. large objective lenses can gather more light and will make the image you see brighter. 12x40 is usually said "12 by 40". also avoid variable magnification images are usually very popr and the zooming mechanism is usually not known for longevity.

i would recommend leopold, zeiss, leica, vortex, meopta, steiner and cabelas euro optics line. these are hard use premiem optics (300-1500 dollars)

still good for the not so serious user are Nikon, budget line of vortex, burris and that about it. the are usually 100 to 400 dollars. personally anything less is kind of a waste.

What i know about optics comes from life long spot and stalk hunting, backcountry hunting and recreational shooting and long range shooting. the optics i use demand durability, versatility and clarity among all else.

if you have more questions or more detail on any matter, let me know.
